claims.text: Polycrystalline single-phase fcc Fe50Co25Ni25 has a grain size of approximately 1–50 µm.
Single-phase fcc Fe50Co25Ni25 has a coercivity of approximately 50 Oe at 300 K.
Single-phase fcc Fe50Co25Ni25 has a saturation magnetization of approximately 1.45 T at 300 K.
Adding 3 at.% B to FeCoNi before casting will produce nanometer-scale boride precipitates segregated at grain boundaries.
Adding B under the specified processing conditions will refine the grain size to no more than approximately 100 nm.
Grain-boundary boride phases act as strong domain-wall pinning centers.
The proposed grain-boundary boride phases raise the effective magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Domain-wall pinning by grain-boundary borides will increase coercivity.
The B-modified alloy will reach a coercivity of approximately 200–300 Oe.
The B-modified alloy will have three to six times the coercivity of the approximately 50 Oe undoped baseline.
The B-modified alloy will retain at least 90% of the original saturation magnetization, corresponding to at least approximately 1.3 T.
The proposed effect applies within a B-content range of 1–5 at.% and a FeCoNi matrix-composition tolerance of ±5 at.%.
The proposed effect applies for final grain sizes of 50–200 nm when measured at 300 K to a maximum field of 1.5 T.
The magnitude of the coercivity increase depends on B content, heat treatment, and final grain size.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies adding 3 at.% B to Fe50Co25Ni25, which would require renormalizing the Fe, Co, and Ni fractions, but the experimental formula Fe47Co24Ni24B3 sums to only 98 at.% and therefore does not define a valid normalized composition.

The processing description lists suction casting into rods and melt spinning into ribbons as though both apply to the same specimens, although these are distinct product geometries and processing routes; separate experimental arms are not defined.
